what_its_for: Candesartan is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and heart failure. Lowering high blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It works by relaxing your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard to pump blood.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor says it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. For high blood pressure in adults, the usual starting dose is 8 mg once a day, and it can be increased up to 32 mg once a day. For heart failure, the starting dose is usually 4 mg once a day. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store candesartan at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using salt substitutes or potassium supplements unless your doctor approves, as this medicine can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness. Do not take non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen or naproxen regularly without talking to your doctor, as they can reduce how well candesartan works and harm your kidneys. Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position to reduce dizziness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (which may be a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); difficulty breathing or swallowing; severe dizziness or fainting; little or no urination; chest pain; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat; or if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Also tell your doctor if you feel very dizzy when standing up or if your blood pressure readings are too low.
when_it_works: You may start to see a small drop in your blood pressure within 2 weeks of starting candesartan. However, it usually takes 4 to 6 weeks to feel the full benefit. Even if you feel well, keep taking this medicine every day. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take candesartan if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby, especially in the second and third trimesters. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if candesartan passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Candesartan can be used in children aged 1 year and older for high blood pressure, but only under a doctor's close supervision. Elderly: Older adults may be more sensitive to dizziness and low blood pressure. Use caution when standing up. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver disease. Always inform your doctor of all medical conditions you have.
